title: Worst-case dynamic Courcelle theorem at bounded treewidth
formal: For every k and fixed CMSO₂ sentence φ, can its truth be maintained deterministically on graphs of treewidth at most k with f(k,φ) log^c(n+2) worst-case update time and O(1) truth queries?
definitions: Use a uniform word-RAM with words of Θ(log(n+2)) bits, unit-cost word arithmetic, Boolean operations, shifts, comparisons and memory accesses, and no nonuniform advice. Constants may be enlarged to address the stated space. The vertex set [n] is fixed, graphs are simple and undirected, and updates insert an absent edge or delete a present edge. Unless stated otherwise the graph starts empty; all outputs must be correct for every legal update sequence. A tree decomposition is a tree of vertex subsets called bags, covering every vertex and edge, such that bags containing any vertex form a connected subtree. Its width is the largest bag size minus one; treewidth is the minimum such width. Every intermediate graph is promised to have treewidth at most k. CMSO₂ is monadic second-order logic in the incidence language with vertex and edge variables, set variables of either sort, equality, incidence, set membership, Boolean connectives and quantifiers, plus predicates |X|≡a (mod b) for fixed integers b≥1,0≤a<b written in φ. The question is Boolean satisfaction, not counting the number of satisfying assignments. The structure may depend on k,φ but must arise from one uniform effective construction. Initialization on the empty graph takes f(k,φ)n^{O(1)} time and space is f(k,φ)n log^c(n+2) words, for computable f and absolute c independent of k,φ. Each individual edge update must meet the bound, not merely its amortized average. Queries return one truth bit. No behavior is required after a promise violation.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of the specified correctness and resource guarantees, or prove that this precise target is impossible. Any conditional impossibility must explicitly state its hypothesis and the implication proved.
context: The 2025 logarithmic-time dynamic treewidth theorem gives amortized bounds; worst-case per-update maintenance is a distinct requirement.
why: A worst-case dynamic Courcelle theorem would make logical tractability stable under every individual update.

import_provenance.original_statement: Under edge insertions and deletions preserving treewidth at most k, can every fixed CMSO₂ graph property be maintained in f(k,φ)·polylog(n) worst-case update time? This is an editorial strengthening of Pilipczuk and coauthors’ dynamic decomposition and logical-property data structures.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The amortized polylogarithmic target was already resolved in 2025; the question specifically asks for a worst-case bound.
